catalog_quote: 1.2 Phonological word. A phonological word is a sequence of syllables marked by the occurrence of primary stress. One syllable particles do not carry primary stress. Phonological words of from one to six syllables have been observed. /pa/ still (particle) /'bɨy/ house /'qu.bɨ/ monkey /ka.'ka.naq/ 'weapon' /tim.ba.ba.'kɨ/ 'thumb' /pig.tu.a.ra.'an/ 'taught' /ki.na.ra.'ya.wan/ 'best' /pig.pa.ka.ra.ku.'a.qan/ 'enlarged' 1.3 Length and stress 1.3.1 Stress carrying length. Stress carries length in open syllables. ('ɨ:.sɨg) child, boy ('pa:.naw) walk (ma.tɨ.'gɨ:) stubborn ... 1.3.2 Degree of stress. There are two degrees of stress, primary (') and secondary ("). A polysyllabic word has one primary stress and if there are three syllables preceding the primary stressed one, also a secondary stress. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote confirmed verbatim on p.192-193 of the held archive.org PDF (page images 2-3), scanned artefacts aside. (2) The deciding source is a 1978 SIL phonemic statement, the sole phonological description of this languoid; nothing better exists per Glottolog (Glottolog's fullest description is a phonology or text collection) and the SIL archive; the complete scan downloaded now adds the title page and the contrast-pair pages, which mark stress phonemically on penult or final syllables and contain no rule conditioning its position, consistent with the 'lexical' (penult~final, unpredictable) coding and the word domain. (3) No list of works to obtain: the remaining Glottolog items are syntax/discourse papers we already hold or a clitic-order thesis; Dawson 1958 and Collins 1970 describe Kalagan/Tagakaulo, not Kaagan.
